title: Mean median and unusual values
goals: Investigate an unusual value before deleting it
Explain how a summary can hide variation

prerequisite.prompt: What is the total of 2, 3 and 4?

vocabulary: Sum of numeric values divided by their count
The middle of sorted values or mean of the two middle values
A value far from most others in a dataset

blocks.text: Five fictional activity durations are 2, 3, 3, 4 and 18 minutes. Most are near 3, but one is much longer. Different summaries reveal different aspects. Keep all values while investigating whether 18 is a genuine long activity or a recording error.

blocks.title: Python 3 code
blocks.text:
values = [2, 3, 3, 4, 18]
ordered = sorted(values)
mean = sum(values) / len(values)
median = ordered[len(ordered) // 2]
print(mean)
print(median)

blocks.title: Follow the evidence
blocks.caption: Read each row from left to right and connect the evidence to the stated rule.

blocks.text: The script prints 6.0 and 3. sorted returns a sorted list without changing the original. This median expression works for a nonempty odd-length list only. For four sorted values, average the second and third. Do not use this odd-length shortcut for every dataset.

blocks.label: Replace 18 with 8. Calculate the new mean and median.

blocks.text: Taking the middle item of an unsorted list can give the wrong median. For [18, 2, 4, 3, 3], the middle item is 4, but the sorted median is 3. Sort first. For an empty list, there is no mean or median under this lesson's rules.
Removing 18 merely because it raises the mean would hide evidence. Check collection notes, keep an audit trail and compare summaries with and without it only with a clear explanation.

blocks.label: A dataset is empty. Is reporting a mean of 0 justified?

workbook.title: Compute two medians
workbook.answer: Sorted first list 1, 3, 9 has median 3. Sorted second 2, 4, 6, 8 has median (4 + 6)/2 = 5.

workbook.title: Repair an explanation
workbook.prompt: A learner deletes 18 because it is above the mean. What evidence is needed before correcting or excluding it?
workbook.answer: Check original measurement and collection rules. Being above the mean alone is not an error. Retain the raw record and document any justified correction.

workbook.title: Compare summaries independently
workbook.prompt: For 1, 2, 2, 3 and 12, calculate mean and median. Then replace 12 with 2 and recalculate. Explain the change.
workbook.answer: Original sum 20, mean 4, median 2. Revised sum 10, mean 2, median 2. The large value changes mean more than median in this example.

workbook.title: Report missing evidence
workbook.prompt: A dataset is empty. Is reporting a mean of 0 justified?
workbook.answer: No. Zero would be a measured summary; no numeric observations are available.

teacher.background: Teach Week 17 as a two-session investigation using fictional data. Five fictional activity durations are 2, 3, 3, 4 and 18 minutes. Most are near 3, but one is much longer. Different summaries reveal different aspects. Keep all values while investigating whether 18 is a genuine long activity or a recording error. Assess the three stated outcomes through the independent task, not by copying the worked result.

Discuss W5 and the exit; use the fresh retry when support was needed.
